answer: At most 5 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a echo tag. The tundra cap is enforced at intake and nadir reveals the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool hence cannot mint a fleet in one epoch regardless of capital it holds, as each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. A farm of 33 pays that 61 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
